headline: Record revenue and EPS on smartphone demand, guiding a ramp
summary_short: Cirrus Logic posted record fiscal Q1 (company label; our shard tracks it as FY2026 Q2) revenue of $459.7M, up 12.9% y/y and 2.5% q/q, with GAAP diluted EPS of $1.47 (+28.9% y/y) on strong smartphone custom-component demand.
summary_long: Revenue grew on strong demand for custom components shipping into smartphones, per CEO John Forsyth, with High-Performance Mixed-Signal up sharply q/q ($210.7M vs $191.3M) while Audio dipped q/q ($249.0M vs $257.2M) but rose y/y. GAAP gross margin held at 52.6% y/y (-0.4ppt q/q) as opex rose to $157.4M on higher R&D. Operating cash flow fell to $64.1M from $116.1M a year ago on working-capital swings (receivables, inventory build). Cash and marketable securities rose to $810.7M (+47.7% y/y). For the next quarter, Cirrus guided revenue of $510M-$570M, GAAP gross margin of 52%-54%, and combined GAAP R&D+SG&A of $163M-$169M (non-GAAP opex $140M-$146M).

drivers.explanation: CEO cited strong demand for custom components shipping into smartphones; High-Performance Mixed-Signal segment revenue rose to $210.7M from $191.3M q/q, offsetting a q/q dip in Audio to $249.0M from $257.2M.
Not explained as a discrete driver in the release; margin held flat y/y at 52.6% but eased 0.4ppt from Q4's 53.0%.
Total operating expenses rose to $157.4M from $147.3M q/q, driven by higher R&D spend ($115.0M vs $107.5M), outpacing gross profit growth.
Fell to $64.1M from $116.1M y/y on working-capital swings including a $33.8M increase in accounts receivable and a $21.9M inventory build, per the cash-flow statement.
Purchases of property, equipment and software rose to $15.1M from $2.6M a year ago; the release gives no qualitative cause beyond the reported figures.

CEO Forsyth called it a record first-quarter revenue and EPS result, citing smartphone custom-component demand, growing interest in the company's AI-PC smart codec, and a newly taped-out analog front-end for metrology applications.
